text:
sam: Customer C-791 escalated — p99 spikes on streaming endpoints (TTFB) vs non-streaming. Sample req id: req_20260317_7a3f. Streaming p99 ~ 3.7s, non-streaming p99 ~ 400ms. Need repro + mitigation.

alex: Can you paste repro steps + curl? Which channel (SSE/h2) and region?

sam: SSE, us-west-2. Repro steps I used:
```
curl -v -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' 'https://api.redwood.cloud/v1/generate?stream=true' --no-buffer --max-time 10
```
Observed: TTFB ~ 3.2s, total ~ 3.4s. Non-streaming test:
```
curl -v -H 'Accept: application/json' 'https://api.redwood.cloud/v1/generate?stream=false' --max-time 10
```
TTFB 0.4s, total 0.42s. Relevant header: X-Request-ID: req_20260317_7a3f
Log snippet:
```
INF 03:12:11 flush_wait=3100ms proxy_write=2ms route=stream-handler req=req_20260317_7a3f
DBG flush_reason=proxy_buffering threshold=16KB current=4KB
```

ops-bot: Alert: streaming-ttfb-surge detected for tenant C-791 (3 events in last 5m). https://internal.redwood/alerts/789

mei: Sounds like proxy coalescing/throttling. nginx/envoy + http2 can buffer small writes until either window/timer/threshold. If runtime writes < proxy threshold you'll see flush_wait. Is this tenant routed via EP-B?

sam: Yes EP-B in us-west-2. Runtime shows flush_wait spikes; proxy_write small but delayed flush.

jordan: Quick checks: 1) Re-run with curl --no-buffer to rule out client buffering; 2) compare h2 path: `curl --http2 -H 'Accept: application/json' ...`; 3) get edge pcap if we need to see window/frame timing.

sam: Re-ran with --no-buffer -> same TTFB. h2 path shows TTFB ~550ms (much better). So SSE path is the problematic one.

mei: Likely EP-B coalescing for SSE to reduce tiny writes. Short-term mitigations:
- Route tenant to EP-A (different edge pool)
- Use non-streaming fallback for latency-sensitive calls (customer is okay with fallback for critical flows)
- Toggle runtime feature flag `flush_immediately=true` for the tenant (needs runtime toggle)

alex: Can ops do a routing override now? Sam, confirm customer accepts brief switch.

sam: Customer OK to try routing to EP-A (no code change). I'll request a routing override in console.

jordan: Engineering follow-ups:
- eng-runtime: check SSE flush path to ensure small writes trigger immediate flush when requested
- eng-edge: audit EP-B proxy config: proxy_buffering, http2 SETTINGS, coalesce timer, proxy_write_timeout
I'll open infra tickets.

ops-bot: Ticket created: INFRA-1429 (edge EP-B coalescing investigation) assigned to @eng-edge.

sam: Temporary routing override applied at 03:16 UTC: tenant moved to EP-A. Early numbers: TTFB dropped to ~480ms. Customer confirmed improvement. Will monitor p95/p99 for 24h.

mei: Add a small e2e smoke test comparing SSE TTFB vs non-streaming TTFB per model/route. Alert if stream_TTFB_p99 > nonstream_TTFB_p99 + 1s.

alex: I'll draft a support doc with repro curl + quick mitigations (routing override, fallback param, feature flag).

sam: Uploaded logs and linked tickets INFRA-1429 and RT-2207 in the customer case. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
